LESSON: PROHIBITIONS IN ISLAM: EVILS OF BEGGING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.1: Prohibitions in Islam: Evils of Begging
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Prohibitions in Islam: Evils of Begging, part of Strand 2 in Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: Why do people beg? 2. Why is begging discouraged?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify categories of people who deserve assistance in society,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prohibitions in Islam: Evils of Begging in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe the evils of begging as a means of fostering hard work,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prohibitions in Islam: Evils of Begging in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate work as a means of eradicating poverty.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prohibitions in Islam: Evils of Begging in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify categories of people who deserve assistance in society,

   Prohibitions in Islam: Evils of Begging helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. describe the evils of begging as a means of fostering hard work,

   Prohibitions in Islam: Evils of Begging helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate work as a means of eradicating poverty.

   Prohibitions in Islam: Evils of Begging helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify categories of people deserving support (debtors, those who lose property through disaster and destitute),

2. discuss evils of begging according to the teachings of Islam and present in class,

3. discuss ways of earning income/ generating income and present in class. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify categories of people deserving support (debtors, those who lose property through disaster and destitute),
2. discuss evils of begging according to the teachings of Islam and present in class,
3. discuss ways of earning income/ generating income and present in class. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Prohibitions in Islam: Evils of Begging together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: the skill of listening and speaking as learners discuss evils of begging according to the

teachings of Islam and present in class.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: the skill of researching as learners discuss ways of earning income/ generating income

and present in class

Values:
• Responsibility enhanced as learners take turns to discuss evils of begging according to the teachings of Islam and present in

class.

• Integrity is enhanced as learners discuss ways of earning income/ generating income and present in class

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life skills: Self-awareness to avoid begging without justification;

Link to other Learning Areas:

Social Studies as learners are encouraged to work and contribute to nation building.
